written.myAnswer: Genetics studies heredity and the transmission of characteristics from parents to offspring. Anatomy studies the internal structure of organisms. Palaeontology studies fossils and ancient life. Marine Biology studies organisms living in the sea. Pathology studies diseases, including their causes and effects.
Embryology is the study of the development of an organism from fertilization to birth or hatching.
Morphology studies the form and structure of organisms; physiology studies how their body parts and systems function.

Dividing biology into branches makes the study of life more manageable and organized. Botany, zoology, and microbiology focus respectively on plants, animals, and microorganisms. Specialization allows researchers to develop detailed knowledge in a particular area and contribute to research and solutions in fields such as health, food, and the environment.
